# SIMP

**S**ymplectic **I**ntegrators for **M**onte-carlo **P**roposals.

SIMP integrates Hamiltonian systems and builds the Hamiltonian Monte
Carlo proposals that run on them. Symplectic integrators conserve a
nearby energy, so a trajectory holds its total energy over long horizons
and the proposals it produces are accepted at high rates.

The integrators are splitting schemes: an alternating sequence of
position and momentum updates whose coefficients define the method.
Leapfrog and the Yoshida order 4, 6, and 8 members come from a single
triple-jump composition, so the whole family shares one stepper and one
coefficient source. Adding a scheme is one registry entry. A two-stage
member, `minerror2`, uses the kick weight `(3 - sqrt(5)) / 4` that
cancels the leading energy error on a Gaussian target, which makes it
the accurate choice for Hamiltonian Monte Carlo on near-Gaussian
posteriors.

For non-separable Hamiltonians, such as Riemannian dynamics with a
position-dependent mass,
[`simp_integrate_nonsep()`](https://gcol33.github.io/SIMP/reference/simp_integrate_nonsep.md)
uses the generalized (implicit) leapfrog.

The steppers are a header-only, scalar-templated C++ core. Consumers
link against it with `LinkingTo: SIMP` and drive it with a native
gradient under automatic differentiation, so the same code path serves
plain-double integration and gradient-based inference engines.

## Install

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("gcol33/SIMP")
```

## Integrate a trajectory

``` r

library(SIMP)

# Unit Gaussian target: U(q) = 0.5 q'q, so grad_U(q) = q.
grad_U <- function(q) q

out <- simp_integrate(
  q0 = c(1, 0), p0 = c(0, 1),
  grad_U = grad_U, eps = 0.1, n_steps = 60,
  integrator = "yoshida4"
)
out$q
```

[`simp_schemes()`](https://gcol33.github.io/SIMP/reference/simp_schemes.md)
lists the built-in integrators with their order and gradient cost per
step.

## Sample with HMC

``` r

Sigma <- matrix(c(1, 0.8, 0.8, 1), 2)
P <- solve(Sigma)
U <- function(q) 0.5 * as.numeric(t(q) %*% P %*% q)
grad_U <- function(q) as.numeric(P %*% q)

fit <- simp_hmc(U, grad_U, init = c(0, 0), n_iter = 2000, eps = 0.2,
                n_steps = 20, warmup = 500, integrator = "leapfrog")

colMeans(fit$draws)
fit$accept_rate
```

Pass any name from
[`simp_schemes()`](https://gcol33.github.io/SIMP/reference/simp_schemes.md)
as `integrator` to compare schemes on the same target.

# Package index

## Integrate

Advance a Hamiltonian trajectory.

- [`simp_integrate()`](https://gcol33.github.io/SIMP/reference/simp_integrate.md)
  : Integrate a Hamiltonian trajectory
- [`simp_integrate_nonsep()`](https://gcol33.github.io/SIMP/reference/simp_integrate_nonsep.md)
  : Integrate a non-separable Hamiltonian (generalized leapfrog)

## Sample

Hamiltonian Monte Carlo built on the integrators.

- [`simp_hmc()`](https://gcol33.github.io/SIMP/reference/simp_hmc.md) :
  Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with a chosen symplectic integrator

## Schemes

The available integrators.

- [`simp_schemes()`](https://gcol33.github.io/SIMP/reference/simp_schemes.md)
  : Available symplectic integrators
